en.title: New Streaming Gems: 'Gentle Monster' to 'The Odyssey' and Powerful Docs Arrive
en.summary: This week's streaming landscape is buzzing with a diverse lineup, from intimate character studies to monumental cinematic events. Dive into new arrivals that promise compelling narratives and thought-provoking perspectives.
en.body:
As the streaming world continues to evolve, new titles consistently emerge, offering fresh narratives for dedicated fans and casual viewers alike. This week brings a compelling mix, from the introspective drama of **Gentle Monster** to the much-anticipated digital release of **The Odyssey**, alongside a powerful documentary that sheds light on a grave injustice.

Marie Kreutzer, the visionary director behind the acclaimed **Corsage**, returns with **Gentle Monster**. Starring **Léa Seydoux** as Lucy, the film opens with a haunting whisper of a '90s pop song, setting a tone of quiet contemplation. Lucy, having transitioned from a life of touring European capitals to a more serene countryside existence, grapples with her new reality. The accompanying piano melody and Seydoux's nuanced performance hint at deeper currents beneath the surface, suggesting a story rich with unspoken emotions and personal adaptation.

## A Glimpse into Injustice and Epic Scope

Beyond the quiet introspection of **Gentle Monster**, this week's arrivals also include **When a Witness Recants**, a profound documentary from director **Dawn Porter**. This film bravely chronicles the decades-long struggle of **Andrew Stewart**, **Ransom Watkins**, and **Alfred Chestnut** – the Harlem Park Three – who spent nearly forty years in prison for a crime they did not commit. With support from **Ta-Nehisi Coates**, who shares a personal connection to the story, the documentary offers a rigorous and deeply affecting examination of the American justice system's failures. Its unforgettable conclusion leaves a lasting impact, highlighting the devastating psychological toll of wrongful imprisonment.

On a grander scale, anticipation is building for **Christopher Nolan**'s **The Odyssey**. While currently a major theatrical release, fans can soon bring this cinematic event home. Digital preorders are available, with the film expected to be available for rent or purchase soon. Following the typical release patterns of Nolan's recent work, a streaming debut is also on the horizon, likely making it accessible on platforms like Peacock in early 2027, offering a chance to re-experience its spectacle from the comfort of one's own home.

## For the Discerning Viewer

The selection this week caters to a wide array of tastes, from those seeking character-driven narratives that explore complex emotions to audiences eager to engage with vital social commentary. **Gentle Monster** promises a nuanced performance from **Léa Seydoux** and Kreutzer's signature directorial touch, while **When a Witness Recants** serves as a crucial reminder of the fight for justice and the resilience of the human spirit. The impending digital release of **The Odyssey** ensures that Nolan's latest blockbuster will soon be accessible to a broader audience, ready to be dissected and discussed by cinephiles worldwide.

## What's Next

Fans can look forward to the digital release of **The Odyssey** for purchase and rent this month, with a Peacock streaming debut anticipated in early 2027. **When a Witness Recants** is currently available to stream on HBO Max, and **Gentle Monster** can be found on VOD platforms.

Roscher’s strong directorial debut Bird in Hand follows a bride-to-be returning to her rural hometown for wedding planning as unresolved tensions crop up. While the plot machinations can feel a bit obvious from the get-go, the performances are universally impressive (particularly from lead Alisha Wainwright), and Roscher proves to have a strong tonal handle on the material, weaving dexterously around complicated feelings of identity and family while injecting a sense of life and humanity in every scene. – Jordan R. Where to Stream: Jolt.film Gentle Monster (Marie Kreutzer) “Look into my eyes / can you see they’re open wide / would I lie to you?” Those lyrics linger in the air as a soft whisper for only a moment before the accompanying piano notes carry them away and into the beginning of Gentle Monster , the latest from Corsage director Marie Kreutzer. One might already suspect that the cover of such an emblematic ’90s pop song, pulsating under the fingertips of the film’s protagonist, Lucy (Léa Seydoux), could serve as exposition in some way. Yet the growl camouflaged in Seydoux’s silky voice might just as well be a sign of fatigue—the Lucy we meet in this opening scene is still adapting to quiet, countryside life from a career of touring European capitals. When her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) interrupts her practice by rushing in, full-on panic attack, it’s the patience in her consoling voice that signals it’s not the first time she has stopped mid-song to make room for him. – Savina P. ( full review ) Where to Stream: Netflix Obsession (Curry Barker) For as wild and uncomfortable as  Obsession  becomes, it is less a question of where the film is going than how it’s going to get there and what path it will take. To Barker’s credit, however, it never feels like he’s stalling for time; a lot of the film is spent observing Bear and his other co-workers, including Sarah (Megan Lawless), the owner’s daughter, who perhaps has a bit of a crush on Bear. Both she and Ian find Nikki’s sudden change a bit odd, concerned that Bear may be taking advantage of a mental breakdown. It’s a development that shows Barker has something on his mind, perhaps recognizing that another version of this movie could be horrific in its misogyny. – Devan S.
